newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply lower but support holds.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply lower but support holds.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended sharply lower in Monday's thin dealings but the benchmark May contract found support below 1,000 stg.

The losses of 13 stg on May to 1,005 stg per tonne, however, left the market vulnerable to a new assault to fill a crucial chart gap between 989-982 stg, traders said. Analysts reckon failure to hold this level may trigger a sell-off.
"I think New York sentiment seems to be that the market will go down to $1,395 and the London sentiment is that it will fill the gap at 982 sterling," said one trader.
"I think the market will continue to come down, backing and filling, and it will go up again," he added.

May bounced off an intraday low of 996 stg but stayed in negative territory throughout the session with sterling's gains against the dollar weighing on London prices. The day's main sellers were said to be Cargill, Credit Lyonnais Rouse and Sucden.

"It's dropped down 18 pounds on the day. It's not too unexpected to find some friendly interest," said the trader. He said the selling included long liquidation by some short-term funds and possibly origins.
Turnover was a slim 3,891 lots, suggesting that the market has not yet shaken off its consolidative mood after last week's spike to 1,048 basis May.

As May edged closer to the gap, traders were on alert for fundamental developments that could steer the market. Some players were looking for a change in the so-far gloomy fundamental picture to prop the market up again.
"If it holds there's still a chance the market can push higher," said Adrian Haylor, technical analyst of Sucden. "If it gets filled, it's a signal of the end off this whole bull move."

One critical factor is the Ivorian midcrop, which could come in lower this year due to weather problems. But analysts in Abidjan said the midcrop was likely to exceed 100,000 tonnes and could even surpass 160,000.
